title: Examination of the Concept of Ecofeminism Using Bibliometric Analysis
content: This study aims to conduct a bibliometric analysis of the literature related to ecofeminism, one of the most significant topics of debate in the 21st century. A Web of Science (WoS) screening of the period 2000-2025 identified 971 articles. Ecofeminism was clearly centered on the social and humanities fields. The most frequently appearing categories were “women’s studies, literature, environmental studies, religion, humanities, interdisciplinary studies, and philosophy”. The United States holds a dominant position in the literature of ecofeminism. After 2023, it appeared that ecofeminism began to attract greater attention at the global level. Six thematic clusters were the “Feminist Environmental Theories and Environmental Ethics”, “Ecology and Ethics”, “Social Justice, Climate Justice, Gender Equality, and Activism”, “Cultural and Spiritual Approaches, Religious Ecology”, “Critiques of Modernization, Development, and Technology”, and finally “Regional and Global Focuses, Local Justice Themes”. The map showed that ecofeminism was situated within three main academic axes: Ethical-philosophical (Ethics and the Environment, Environmental Ethics, Feminist Theory, etc.), education and sustainability (Journal of Environmental Education, Sustainability), and cultural-theological (Feminist Theology, Environmental Communication, Humanities-Basel. In conclusion, the literature of ecofeminism has gone beyond being merely an environmental ethics approach and it has evolved into a multidimensional field of research encompassing sustainability, climate justice, and eco-political solidarity.
